title.narrative: Community-Based GBV, CP and MA Services in Washokani, Serekaniye, and Tal Samen

description.narrative: ltpgtltbrgtBahar Organization proposes a seven-month integrated protection response in Washokani, Serekaniye, and Tal Samen camps, addressing the urgent needs of internally displaced women, girls, boys, and other at-risk groups. The intervention will establish three dedicated Community Centers within the camps to serve as inclusive and confidential spaces where vulnerable individuals—particularly children and GBV survivors—can safely access protection services and tailored support.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe project will focus on delivering survivor- and child-centered services in the areas of Gender-Based Violence (GBV) and Child Protection (CP). These services will include structured case management and mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) for children at risk of abuse, exploitation, or recruitment, as well as for GBV survivors. Complementary activities such as awareness-raising on protection risks and parenting programs will help caregivers build safer environments for children and adolescents.ltbrgtlt/pgtltbrgtRecognizing the importance of empowerment in mitigating protection risks, the project will provide targeted empowerment activities for women, girls, and boys, including life skills training, recreational programs, and group discussions to build self-confidence, resilience, and agency. Life skills programs will cover topics such as decision-making, conflict resolution, leadership, hygiene management, and financial literacy, tailored to the needs of adolescent girls and boys. Youth will also benefit from targeted MHPSS interventions focusing on emotional well-being, coping strategies, and trauma recovery. In addition, child and adolescent survivors of GBV will receive specialized case management (CM) services with a strong emphasis on confidentiality, survivor agency, and age-appropriate interventions.ltbrgtltpgtltbrgtTo strengthen community ownership and sustainability, Bahar will facilitate the establishment of camp-level CP and GBV networks, enhancing early identification of risks, improving referral pathways, and reinforcing localized protection systems. Capacity building is also central to the intervention, with tailored training for CP and GBV professionals, non-specialist staff, and community volunteers, ensuring a quality, sensitive, and inclusive service approach.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThis project will be implemented in close coordination with the Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC), whose intervention overlaps geographically and complements Bahar’s work. While NRC leads on general protection and legal services—delivered via mobile teams—Bahar will focus on GBV and CP programming within fixed community centers. An effective referral pathway will be established to ensure seamless collaboration between the two organizations. NRC has also expressed interest in utilizing Bahar’s community centers when needed, strengthening operational complementarity and maximizing the use of available resources.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThrough this coordinated and multi-sectoral approach, Bahar aims to restore critical protection services, empower displaced communities, and support a safer, more dignified path toward recovery and voluntary return in the evolving Syrian context.lt/pgt
